name: hcapp_sendRoomMessage
description: Posts to a platform-wide chat room — one of the rooms in HC6.ChatRoomCatalog(), scoped to no kennel or run. The message is an HC.EventMessage row with EventId, KennelId and ThreadId all NULL and MessageType naming the room (no new table or column: James, 2026-09-13/14). Auth: HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 104, @param NULL — a standard token). Permission gate: HC6.UserMayEnterChatRoom(@userId, @roomType) — the one gate shared with hcapp_getRoomMessages and hcapp_getChatRooms, so the three cannot drift; an unknown room returns 0 and is refused (1942, errorType 13). NOT HC6.CheckKennelPermission, because a room belongs to no kennel. Returns the message in the flutter_chat_core shape (rowset 0, parsed by two clients and unchanged), then API-only push plumbing: push detail (1), visible recipients (2) and silent recipients (3). Rowsets 1–3 are computed inside a log-and-swallow TRY so a push-side failure never fails a send that has already committed. Room push audience is every hasher UserMayEnterChatRoom admits whose HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts.ParticipationState for the room is 0 (push, the default — no row means 0) or 1 (badges only); 2 (opted out) gets nothing. Unlike kennel/event bells, 0 IS consent here: a hasher only has the room because they hold its role. Since 2026-10-13 a resend of an already-stored @messageId by the same sender in the same thread is idempotent: nothing is written, rowset 0 returns the stored message and the push rowsets are empty, so nobody is notified twice (a resend after a lost reply used to hit PK_EventMessage and report a delivered message as unsent). Since 2026-10-13 its MERGE into HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts holds HOLDLOCK: the table has no unique key on (UserId, EventId, KennelId, ThreadId, MessageType), and two concurrent MERGEs could each insert a row.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Registered device UUID. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully).

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived token (standard, device secret; @param NULL). Default NULL.

parameters.name: roomType
parameters.description: The room, as HC6.ChatRoomCatalog().RoomType. Required; NULL → 1941. Unknown or not admitted → 1942.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: Client-generated message UUID. Required; NULL → 1941. A duplicate id is a PK violation caught by the CATCH (1943) — the insert is not idempotent.

parameters.name: messageContent
parameters.description: Message body. Required; LEN() = 0 → 1941 (LEN, not = '', so an emoji-only message passes — a surrogate pair has no sort weight in this collation and N'<emoji>' = '' is TRUE). More than 4,000 UTF-16 code units (the column width) is REFUSED with 1942 rather than truncated; the parameter is MAX for that reason.

parameters.name: messageKind
parameters.description: 0 text (default), 1 photo, 2 location (E9.F1.S11/S12). NULL → 0. Validated by HC6.ChatMessageKindError; a bad pairing → 1944.

parameters.name: replyToMessageId
parameters.description: The message this one quotes (E9.F1.S21). Kept only when it is a message of THIS room (EventId/KennelId/ThreadId NULL and MessageType = @roomType); otherwise silently cleared.

rowsets.description: Returned alone, then RETURN, on: auth failure (from ValidateAppAuth); 1941 missing roomType/messageId/content (errorType 2); 1942 content over 4,000 (errorType 2) — AND 1942 not admitted to the room (errorType 13; the same code is reused for two different refusals, only errorType tells them apart); 1944 bad message kind (2); 1943 unhandled error in the write transaction (5).

rowsets.name: Message
rowsets.description: On success: the message in the shape the chat page already reads for kennel and event threads (flutter_chat_core). One row. UNCHANGED since 2026-09-13 apart from the additive messageKind and canDelete.

columns.name: id
columns.description: UPPER(EventMessage.id). Uppercase on purpose — the client lowercases on arrival (HcId).

columns.name: type
columns.description: Always 'text' — even for a photo or location; messageKind carries the kind.

columns.name: text
columns.description: EventMessage.MessageContent — the raw content (text, photo URL or map link).

columns.name: roomId
columns.description: Always the empty GUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 — a room has no id in this column; the client knows the room from the call it made.

columns.name: createdAt
columns.description: EventMessage.createdAt as Unix epoch milliseconds (DATEDIFF_BIG from 1970-01-01; createdAt is sysutcdatetime).

columns.name: authorFirstName
columns.description: Hasher.DisplayName (hash name or real name per preference).

columns.name: canDelete
columns.description: Always 1 — it is the sender's own message.

rowsets.name: PushDetail
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY (stripped before the reply): what the shim needs to build the push. One row. Inside the log-and-swallow TRY — absent, together with rowsets 2–3, if that section fails.

columns.name: RoomName
columns.description: HC6.ChatRoomCatalog().RoomName (LEFT JOIN — NULL only for a room not in the catalog, which the gate already refused).

columns.name: MessageTitle
columns.description: RoomName + ' — ' + DisplayName (NULL if RoomName is NULL).

columns.name: MessageContent
columns.description: HC6.ChatMessagePreview(MessageKind, MessageContent) — the push body, not the raw URL for a photo/location.

rowsets.name: VisiblePushRecipients
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY: one row per distinct FCM token of a hasher admitted by HC6.UserMayEnterChatRoom whose room ParticipationState is 0 (no row = 0). Device must be live (removed 0, token present, LastLogin within 180 days, build >= HC6.MinBuildForChatPush() via TRY_CAST — fails closed) and the hasher must not have blocked the sender (HasherFriendMap.Ignore). The sender's own devices ARE included (the echo drives the delivered tick; James 2026-09-18). May be empty. HC6.UserMayEnterChatRoom is evaluated per hasher in the WHERE (line 320).

columns.name: BadgeTotal
columns.description: HC6.UserUnreadChatTotal for the recipient (app-icon badge); NULL when no device with that token is on a build >= HC6.MinBuildForIconBadge().

rowsets.name: SilentPushRecipients
rowsets.description: On success, API ONLY: the same audience with ParticipationState 1 (participate, badges only) — a data-only push. Same columns as rowset 2. May be empty.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.EventMessage (EventId, KennelId, ThreadId NULL; MessageType = @roomType; MessageTitle ''; MessageReleasabilityFlags 63) — fires HC.trgCreateSeqNum (MessageSequenceCount) and HC.trgEventMessageActivityCount (no-op: EventId NULL).

MERGE HC.EventMessageBadgeCounts keyed on (UserId, EventId NULL, KennelId NULL, ThreadId NULL, MessageType = @roomType) — the sender's last-read position moves to the new sequence number. IS NULL predicates, not =, so no duplicate rows per message.
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on every refused path, in the write CATCH, and in the push-plumbing CATCH ('Push audience failed in sendRoomMessage', swallowed).
The API shim fans out FCM pushes from rowsets 2 and 3; nothing is queued in the database.

codeSmells.detail: Line 117 returns 1942 for 'Message too long' (errorType 2) and line 150 returns 1942 for 'Not authorised' to the room (errorType 13). Any client or log triage keyed on the errorCode alone conflates a length refusal with a permission refusal. The sibling SPs use distinct codes (1902 vs none, 2011 vs 2013).

codeSmells.issue: Per-row scalar function in the audience WHERE
codeSmells.detail: Line 320 calls HC6.UserMayEnterChatRoom(h.id, @roomType) for every (hasher × device) row of HC.Hasher JOIN HC.Device that passes the other predicates. It is a small gate by design (CLAUDE.md allows row-at-a-time gates) but the driving set is the whole hasher table, not a room roster, so cost grows with the user base, not the room.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
